controls.title: Manage identities and accounts through their lifecycle
controls.statement: Create, change, disable and remove human and non-human identities through documented processes tied to an authorised business need.
controls.risk: Accounts that remain active without a current owner or purpose can be used to enter systems without attracting attention or clear accountability.
controls.scope: Workforce, contractor, service, application and device identities and their associated accounts.
controls.examine: Compare personnel, contractor and service records with account inventories, provisioning approvals, role changes, expiry dates and deprovisioning records.
controls.interview: Ask identity and system owners how joiners, movers, leavers, temporary access and non-human identities enter the lifecycle process.
controls.test: Sample newly created, changed, expired and terminated identities and trace whether each account was authorised, updated and disabled within the applicable timeframe.
test_steps: Select human, contractor, service, application and device identities covering new starters, transfers, temporary access, expiry and termination.
Trace each identity to an authorised owner and purpose, verified source record, provisioning approval, assigned accounts and lifecycle dates.
Compare role-change and termination times with live accounts, sessions, tokens and downstream directories to verify changes reached every connected system on time.
Attempt a safe sign-in with sampled expired or terminated credentials and confirm denial, logging and removal of residual access.
controls.expected: Every sampled account has a current owner and purpose, follows the approved lifecycle process and is disabled or removed when no longer required.

mappings.basis: Requires appropriate user lifecycle management supporting personnel management.
Requires formal, documented and accountable provisioning for human and non-human identities and addresses dormant accounts.
Requires approved creation, enablement, modification, monitoring, disabling and removal of accounts.
Requires an account inventory and recurring validation of active accounts, supporting lifecycle control without specifying the full workflow.
Covers provisioning identities for personnel, services and devices.
Covers deprovisioning identities when they are no longer required.

controls.title: Approve and review access rights
controls.statement: Grant access only after accountable approval, keep permissions aligned with current duties and review them when roles or risk conditions change.
controls.risk: People and services can accumulate access they no longer need, increasing the damage possible from error, misuse or a compromised account.
controls.scope: Logical access rights, roles, entitlements and authorisations for enterprise systems and information.
controls.examine: Inspect access policies, owner approvals, role definitions, access-review results, exceptions and evidence that identified excess access was removed.
controls.interview: Ask business and system owners how they decide what access is appropriate and how they respond to transfers, temporary assignments and review findings.
controls.test: Sample access grants and review decisions, compare permissions with current duties and verify that rejected or obsolete access was removed.
test_steps: Select access grants, denials, retained entitlements and removals from high-risk and ordinary systems, including inherited group and role access.
Compare each effective permission with current duties, data or system owner approval, segregation rules, start and expiry dates and the latest review decision.
For access marked removed or reduced, query the target system and attempt a benign authorised action to confirm the obsolete capability is gone.
Recalculate a review population from live entitlements and record missing accounts, unsupported retention or decisions made by an unauthorised reviewer.
controls.expected: Sampled access is owner-approved, matches current responsibilities and has been reviewed and corrected at defined triggers.

mappings.basis: Requires regular verification that human and non-human access remains required and appropriate, including after role changes.
Requires permissions, entitlements and authorisations to be defined, managed, enforced and reviewed.
Requires logical access requests to be reviewed and approved by the asset owner.
Requires periodic and trigger-based review and updating of logical access privileges.
Requires a defined process for granting access after hiring, rights grants and role changes.
Requires account approvals, authorised users, role membership, access authorisations and ongoing account management.

controls.title: Protect and manage authentication credentials
controls.statement: Issue, store, use, change and revoke passwords, keys, certificates and other authenticators through controlled processes appropriate to their risk.
controls.risk: Poorly protected or unmanaged credentials can let an attacker impersonate a trusted user or service and retain access after the credential should have been revoked.
controls.scope: Passwords, authentication secrets, tokens, certificates and other authenticators for people, services and devices.
controls.examine: Review authenticator standards, issue and recovery procedures, approved storage, default-credential handling, compromise response and revocation records.
controls.interview: Ask identity and platform owners how recipients are verified, credential strength is selected and lost, exposed or expired credentials are handled.
controls.test: Sample authenticators across user, service and device accounts and verify controlled issue, protected storage, required changes and effective revocation.
test_steps: Sample passwords, tokens, certificates, keys and device credentials across issue, recovery, rotation, compromise, expiry and revocation states.
Verify recipient or device identity checks, approved strength, protected delivery and storage, ownership, expiry and recovery controls for each sample.
Use an authorised test credential before and after rotation or revocation to confirm the new authenticator works and the old one no longer grants access.
Trace issue, recovery and revocation events to audit records and confirm exposed or default credentials trigger the documented response.
controls.expected: Sampled authenticators are issued to verified recipients, protected according to policy and promptly changed or revoked when their trust is lost.

mappings.basis: Requires controls for authenticator issue, strength, distribution, default values, compromise and revocation.
Requires secure storage and handling of credentials and encryption keys, including centrally managed credential storage.
Requires identities and credentials for authorised users, services and hardware to be managed.
Covers issuing passwords, smartcards, certificates and keys to entities requiring access.
